Use it together with a release target label; on its own it does nothing, because the release job runs only when there is at least one target. release:no-propagate-dependents Do not add transitive dependents to the release plan.

A label has to exist in the repository before it can be added to a pull request. Only some release labels are defined, and the set changes as maintainers add them. List the current ones with:

gh label list --search "release:"

If the label you need is missing (for example release:dry-run or release:ai_core:minor), ask a maintainer to create it with exactly that name.

Rules enforced by .github/scripts/parse_release_labels.py and the planner:

  • A pull request may carry several release labels. If one module appears more than once, the highest bump wins (major over minor over patch).
  • A label naming a module that does not exist fails the run early. A target tag that already exists on the remote is skipped with a log line (Tag ... already exists; skipping) rather than failing the run, so if a release seems to have done nothing, check the workflow summary.
  • Labels must match release:<name>:<patch|minor|major>. A label that does not match is ignored without an error, so a typo such as release:auth:ptach releases nothing and does not fail the run. Check the plan in the workflow summary.

docs.title: PR Merged Module Releases (pr-merged-module-releases.yml)
docs.text:
Runs when a pull request is closed as merged and its base branch is dev or matches dev-<major>.<minor>.x. Steps:

  1. Parse the release labels, the changed modules and the PR body.
  2. Refuse to continue if any pyproject.toml still contains rev = "dev".
  3. Plan the release. A module whose version the PR already bumped by the requested level is released in tag_only mode. Otherwise the automation bumps it itself in auto_bump mode.
  4. Apply every auto_bump change and push them in one commit.
  5. Create the new tags from that final commit, so every tag created in this run points at one commit SHA, then create GitHub Releases. A tag that already exists is skipped and keeps the commit it was created on.

Dependents are included by default. If a release includes core, every module that depends on core (directly or transitively) is patch-bumped, has its pinned rev rewritten to the new tag, and is released after its upstream modules.

The bulk commit message and the release commits are marked [skip ci], so they do not start the CI workflows again.

docs.title: Module Release (module-release-tags.yml)
docs.text:
A manual workflow_dispatch workflow (also callable as a reusable workflow) for releasing one module on demand. Inputs:

Input Notes module core or a folder under modules/. Anything else is rejected with the list of valid names. bump patch, minor, major or none. create_github_release Default true. release_notes Optional text for the GitHub Release body. target_branch Default same as active branch. The branch must exist on origin.

It uses Poetry to bump the version, patch-bumps and retags dependent modules, commits with chore(release): <module> <bump> to v<version> [skip ci], pushes to the target branch, then creates tags and GitHub Releases. The run aborts if the target branch moved after it started, except in recovery mode (below).

bump: none is recovery mode. It recreates a missing tag or GitHub Release without changing the version again. If the branch moved since the run started, recovery mode switches to the latest remote head instead of aborting, so it can tag a newer commit than the one checked out when the run began. It still collects dependents so the release set stays consistent.

docs.title: Release Branch Guard (release-branch-guard.yml)
docs.text: Runs on pull requests (opened, reopened, synchronized, edited) and calls .github/scripts/validate_release_branches.py. It fails when dev does not exist, when no stabilization branch matching dev-<major>.<minor>.x exists, or when the pull request's base branch does not exist.

docs.title: How versions and tags are produced
docs.text:
• The version lives in the module's own pyproject.toml ([tool.poetry] version). Poetry (1.8.3 in CI) applies the bump.
  • The tag is <dir>-v<version>, created on the commit that carries the bump.
  • GitHub Releases are created by the workflows. Release notes come from the PR body, described next.

docs.title: Release notes in the PR body
docs.text:
The workflow reads a ## Release Notes section from the merged pull request body (heading case-insensitive). The organisation-wide pull request template already includes this section; remove it from PRs that do not carry a release:* label.

## Release Notes

General notes that appear in every module release from this PR.

### auth

Notes for the auth release only.

### core

Notes for the core release only.

Text before the first ### <module> heading is general and goes into every released module. Each ### <module> section goes only to that module. Names may be wrapped in backticks. General notes come first, and both are added before the generated release metadata. With no section, the release body is only the generated metadata.

docs.title: How modules pin each other
docs.text:
Every module depends on core and sometimes on other modules through a Poetry git dependency pinned to a release tag. From modules/auth/pyproject.toml:

msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev="core-v0.2.1" }

Rules:

  • The rev is always a release tag in the form <dir>-v<version>. Never commit rev = "dev". The release workflows run release_checks.py ensure-no-dev-pins and stop if they find one.
  • When a release publishes a new version of a package, the release automation rewrites the rev in every dependent module and patch-bumps the dependent, then tags it after its upstream. You normally do not edit these pins by hand.
  • Local development ignores the pins. During the install, scripts/install_modules.py points them at the local packages and restores the files afterwards: a package installed in the same run is referenced by name, so pip resolves it to the editable directory it was given; any other local package is referenced as a local editable path. See Contributing.

docs.title: Release commits
docs.text: Automated release commits carry [skip ci] and a chore(release): ... message, for example chore(release): bump ai_core, documents, knowledge, ai_api [skip ci]. They only touch pyproject.toml version lines and pinned rev values. If you rebase a branch over them, keep the version and pin changes.

docs.title: Versions in this repository
docs.text: dev is the branch for the v0.2.x line and later. Older minor lines are maintained on dev-<major>.<minor>.x branches, for example dev-0.1.x. The 0.2.x packages require Pydantic v2: core/pyproject.toml declares pydantic = ">=2.8,<3".

docs.title: Doing a release as a contributor
docs.text:
1. Open the pull request against dev.
  2. Add the release:<module>:<bump> label (or a wildcard label), creating it first if it does not exist, and fill in ## Release Notes if you want custom notes. For a new module, set the version you want released (for example 0.1.0) in its pyproject.toml; the label's bump does not change it.
  3. Merge. The release workflows run only after the pull request is merged, so there is no pre-merge preview. A pull request merged with release:dry-run and a release target label makes the run compute and validate the plan and write it to the workflow summary, without committing, tagging or publishing.
  4. For a real release, merge without release:dry-run. The workflow bumps, tags and publishes. Do not push tags by hand.

docs.title: Writing docs
docs.text: This site is built with MkDocs and the Material theme. These pages explain how the site is organised, how to build it, and the rules every page follows.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
Everything lives in docs/, and mkdocs.yml at the repository root controls the build (docs_dir: ./docs, output in ./doc-site).

Directory Audience and content docs/index.md Site home. docs/modules/ One page per module, written to the module page template. docs/quick-start/ The basics path for new integrators. docs/integration/ Deeper guides on extending and wiring MSFLib. docs/concepts/ Cross-cutting concepts. docs/reference/ API reference entry point. docs/contributing/ This contributor section.

docs.title: Navigation is hand-written
docs.text:
The nav: block in mkdocs.yml is a hand-written list. A page that exists in docs/ but is not listed in nav: is built but does not appear in the sidebar, and mkdocs build --strict reports it. To add a page:

  1. Create the Markdown file under the right directory in docs/.
  2. Add an entry to nav: in mkdocs.yml, in the same section, for example - Writing docs: contributing/writing-docs.md.
  3. Build with --strict (below) and fix every warning.

docs.title: Build locally
docs.text:
Install the tools into a virtual environment:

pip install -r requirements-docs.txt

That file lists MkDocs, Material and mkdocstrings[python], which builds the API reference.

Build the site. --strict turns warnings, such as broken links and pages missing from the nav, into errors:

mkdocs build --strict

Preview with live reload:

mkdocs serve

A plain mkdocs build writes to doc-site/ in the repository root, which is git-ignored. To build somewhere else, pass -d <dir>.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
The pages under docs/reference/ are generated, and checked in. Each holds ::: directives that mkdocstrings expands from the docstrings in the source at build time, so changing a docstring needs no regeneration. Adding a public module or package does:

python scripts/gen_api_reference.py

The script discovers core/msflib/* and each tracked modules/<name>/msflib/<name> package, rewrites the pages, removes pages it no longer generates, and exits non-zero if a generated page is missing from the nav in mkdocs.yml. Add that nav entry by hand, then commit the regenerated pages. Members named tests, test_* and conftest are filtered out in mkdocs.yml. The reference shows only members that have a docstring, so a package with few docstrings shows little on its page.

docs.title: Module pages
docs.text: Every page under docs/modules/ follows the module page template: Purpose, Install, Wiring into a host app, Configuration, Key concepts, Examples, Troubleshooting, API reference and See also, in that order. Leave out a section only when it does not apply.

docs.title: Writing rules
docs.text:
• Describe the code as it behaves today. Do not document planned behavior as if it exists. If something is planned, say so once and link to the tracking issue. Where the code differs from the intended behaviour, add a linked notice as described in Documenting known issues.
  • Verify every snippet. Check each command, import, setting name and signature against the source or the tests, or run it. Never copy from older prose without checking it.
  • Install samples pin release tags, for example rev = "core-v0.2.1", and never rev = "dev". Look up the current tag in the module's pyproject.toml or with git tag. See Releases.
  • Use relative links between pages (../concepts/policy.md, not full URLs). Every link target must exist. mkdocs build --strict catches broken page links.
  • Write plain, direct prose. State what a thing does, then how to use it. Skip filler and marketing language.
  • Do not use emojis.
  • Put commands in fenced code blocks with a language tag, one command per block where practical.
  • Do not hand-write signature tables for the API. Link to the reference section instead.

docs.title: Checks and publishing
docs.text:
The docs-check workflow (.github/workflows/docs-check.yml) runs on pull requests against dev that touch docs/, mkdocs.yml, requirements-docs.txt, scripts/gen_api_reference.py, core/, modules/ or the workflow file itself. It regenerates the API reference and fails if that changes or adds any file, builds the site with mkdocs build --strict, and runs a link check over docs/**/*.md.

The site is published to msflib/docsite under fastapi/ by .github/workflows/deploy-openwiki-mkdocs.yml, which calls the shared deploy workflow in msflib/devops. It runs on a push to dev that touches docs/, mkdocs.yml, requirements-docs.txt, core/ or modules/, and on workflow_dispatch from the Actions tab. Merging a docs change to dev therefore publishes it; there is nothing to run by hand.

The repository also has a generated openwiki/ index, refreshed by .github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml. That workflow runs only on workflow_dispatch (its push trigger is commented out). Do not edit those generated pages by hand.

docs.title: Coding guidelines
docs.text:
These pages are the conventions for writing and reviewing code in MSFLib. They apply equally to people and to coding agents (Claude Code, Copilot, Codex, Gemini). The repository-root AGENTS.md is the short entry point for agents and links back here.

The source code and tests are authoritative. When a guideline and established code disagree, raise it rather than silently following either.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: Page Prefix Covers Architecture and scoping ARC, SCP core vs modules, layering, cross-module dependencies, scope Module authoring MOD folder layout, __init__.py, config, eventbus, pipelines, READMEs Models and schemas MDL SQLModel tables, Create/Update/Read schemas, scope columns, enums, relationships Actions and services SVC what goes in action classes vs services, transactions, events HTTP boundary API router factories, deps.py, request and response shapes Typing and contracts TYP typed objects, Protocols, boundary validation Dependencies and packaging DEP optional extras, installs, releases Readiness checks RDY engine, checks and remedies, masking, the migration gate, vetting a readiness PR Testing TST running tests, fixtures, live-service isolation Self-documenting code SDC naming of modules, functions, variables and classes; structure that explains itself Style and change policy STY linting, comments, clean breaks, scope discipline Reviewing pull requests REV review checklist, triaging bot findings, fix commits Working as an agent AGT planning, asking, validating, where plans live Known pitfalls — gotchas that have already cost time

docs.title: Rule IDs
docs.text:
Every rule has a stable ID such as SVC-4. Cite IDs in review comments and commit messages ("fixes SVC-4: drop commit passthrough"). IDs are never reused: when a rule is retired, mark it Retired and leave the heading in place.

Each rule is stated as a short imperative, followed where useful by Why and a reference implementation in the codebase.

docs.title: Changing the guidelines
docs.text:
• A new convention agreed in a PR review is added to the relevant page in the same PR (REV-6).
  • Take the next free number in the page's prefix.
  • Keep rules short. Long rationale belongs in a tracking issue or the module's architecture notes, linked from the rule.

docs.title: SVC-1 · All database access goes through ModelAction
docs.text:
• Every table has an action class extending msflib.actions.ModelAction[Model, Create, Update].
  • Mutations go through super().create/update/delete (with decorator= and commit=) so ModelBase lifecycle events fire. Never session.add() a row from a service or router.
  • Services use an existing action instead of querying the session directly.

Known gap

auth/router.py sets last_login_date on login with session.add() and session.commit() directly. Don't copy it; it needs its own change to go through the account action.

docs.title: SVC-2 · Actions hold only database concerns
docs.text:
Keep in the action: query construction (filters, ordering, joins) and write concurrency mechanics (nested transactions, IntegrityError fallbacks). Move domain policy (retry backoff, state transitions) into a function in services/ and pass the result to update/create.

Delete action methods that only reshape **filters into get_by_all or wrap self.update with a computed dict (mark_done); call the base method instead. Don't coerce types inside actions; shape the models and schemas so data arrives typed.

docs.title: SVC-3 · Multi-dimension scoped queries take the typed scope object
docs.text: A query filtering on two or more scope dimensions takes the module's scope contract (a TenantScope subclass such as ConversationScope or KnowledgeScope) as one parameter, not a growing list of scalars. The request boundary builds it once (SCP-4) and each layer passes it on unchanged; only the action unpacks it into column filters. A single scalar such as tenant_id is fine when only one dimension applies.

docs.title: SVC-4 · Each service function is one closed unit of work
docs.text:
A service function commits itself and takes no commit: bool parameter.

An exception needs a named, current caller that composes it with another call in one transaction, documented in the function's docstring. Before adding commit=False anywhere, grep for callers that pass it; an unused commit parameter should be removed.

Documented exceptions to follow: KnowledgeEngine.ingest (commit=False joins a larger caller transaction, deferring its post-commit work) and IngestionDispatchService.enqueue_and_dispatch_created (commit=False with dispatch_after_commit for a caller that owns the outer transaction). Don't flag a documented commit parameter like these as a violation.

Under review

documents/services/uploads.py upload_file() keeps a commit parameter whose only caller passes commit=True.

docs.title: SVC-5 · Compose multi-row writes on the action, or inside one service method
docs.text:
• Several rows that form one database concern (create a conversation with its owner membership and event) are one action method that uses commit=False internally and commits once.
  • When a service must combine actions atomically (get-or-create a thread, then post a reply), keep both calls in that one service method: the first call uses commit=False, the second commits, and a failure path calls session.rollback() and re-raises. Never compose transactions in the router.
  • A cross-module unit of work (blob storage + a documents action + an ingestion dispatch) is the legitimate case for a service-level composition.

docs.title: SVC-6 · Services with dependencies are classes with constructor injection
docs.text:
A service that needs actions or settings is a class that receives them in __init__ (defaulting to new instances). session and per-call data (scope, participant, rows) stay method arguments. Pure predicates over loaded rows stay plain functions. Reference: conversation/services/, ai_core/services/ingestion_pipeline.py.

Name a constructor argument for what it holds: a service taking already-scoped ConversationSettings uses conversation_settings=, not settings=, which elsewhere means the raw host settings.

docs.title: SVC-7 · Resolve default collaborators lazily when they form a cycle
docs.text: If default-constructing a collaborator in __init__ would construct back to the current class (ConversationAction → MemberAction → MessageAction), store None and resolve it on first use inside the method.

docs.title: SVC-8 · Pass the boundary schema through unchanged
docs.text:
A Create/Update built at the boundary flows to the action as the same object (data: MessageCreate). Don't unpack it into scalar parameters in the service and rebuild it in the action. Pass service-computed additions alongside it via update= or data.model_copy(update=...).

  • Single-field operations (mark_read(up_to_message_id)) keep a plain scalar.
  • For an Update shared by several operations, project one operation's fields with data.model_dump(exclude_unset=True, include={...}), not per-field if x is not None blocks.

docs.title: SVC-9 · Return related rows you just created
docs.text: A create method that also inserts a related row may return tuple[Model, Related] (or Related | None) so callers don't re-query it. Retrofitting this onto existing call sites is a larger change; confirm before starting.

docs.title: SVC-10 · Defer events until commit
docs.text:
When a write uses commit=False, emit its event with msflib.actions.emit_after_commit(session, event, instance, payload) so listeners never see uncommitted state. Don't hand-roll paired sqlalchemy.event.listen(..., once=True) callbacks.

Listeners receive (instance, payload), not a session. Payloads carry public ids and scope values so listeners can act without re-querying.

docs.title: SVC-11 · Put each check in the layer that owns it
docs.text:
Check Where Access decisions, including "this membership belongs to this conversation" access predicates (services/access.py) Another entity belongs to the conversation (message, thread, resource) inline in the service Consistency between rows the action already has in memory inline in the action, only when no extra query is needed

Don't inject an extra action just to re-check something the caller already validated. Don't create a shared module for a single comparison.

docs.title: Working as an agent
docs.text: These rules apply to any coding agent working in this repository. Most also apply to people.

docs.title: AGT-1 · Read before writing
docs.text: Read AGENTS.md and the guideline pages that cover the area you are changing. Look at how existing modules solve the same problem before inventing a new pattern, and name the reference you followed.

docs.title: AGT-2 · Present a plan before architecture-level changes
docs.text:
When a change redistributes responsibility across files or layers (where checks live, how layers call each other, module boundaries), stop after the investigation and present the plan: files touched, what changes in each, what stays. Wait for an explicit go-ahead. An answer to a narrower question earlier in the conversation doesn't approve the whole plan.

Straightforward bug fixes with an obvious, local resolution don't need this.

docs.title: AGT-3 · Ask when the decision belongs to the maintainer
docs.text: Ask before choosing compatibility shim or clean break (STY-4), before refactors with a large blast radius, and before anything outward-facing (pushing, opening or commenting on PRs and issues).

docs.title: AGT-4 · Check rationale against the code
docs.text: Before accepting a docstring or comment's claim about why something is designed a certain way, grep for real consumers. "Kept separate for architectural reasons" can be a leftover that was never reconciled.

docs.title: AGT-5 · Validate narrowly and report faithfully
docs.text: Run the narrowest check that proves the change (TST-1). Report failures with their full output. Don't describe work as done or verified unless it was.

docs.title: AGT-6 · Where plans live
docs.text:
• work/ is a private, gitignored scratch area for planning notes. Nothing there is shared, so never cite it as a source in committed code or docs.
  • Architecture plans meant to be shared become GitHub tracking issues.
  • Content that must be versioned moves from work/ into a tracked location (for example these pages).

docs.title: AGT-7 · Branching and merges
docs.text: Branch from dev; target dev. Write PR descriptions from the org template (REV-7). When syncing a long-lived branch with dev, first diff the branch's own commit range to find which conflicted files it actually touched; files it never changed can take dev's side.

docs.title: AGT-8 · Stay in scope
docs.text: Follow STY-6. When you notice an unrelated issue, report it instead of fixing it.

docs.title: API-1 · Routers are factory functions with injected dependencies
docs.text: router(*, get_session, get_current_account, ..., prefix="", tags=None) -> APIRouter. The host app supplies session, auth, workspace and tenant resolvers; modules hold no app models or session globals. Router factories take keyword-only parameters. Reference: conversation/router.py, ai_api/router/.

docs.title: API-2 · Extract deps.py once a router has real guard logic
docs.text: When a router does more than one or two trivial checks, move request-scoped resolution into a deps.py factory returning a DependencyNamespace: principal, participant, and access-checked context objects (frozen dataclasses of row, conversation, membership) resolved from path parameters. The router factory accepts dependencies= and injectable services as override points. Reference: ai_api/deps.py, conversation/deps.py.

docs.title: API-3 · No anonymous surface on protected endpoints
docs.text: A router that serves protected endpoints takes get_current_account as a required parameter, and every protected endpoint depends on it. A missing account, or one without an id, returns 401, not 403. Authentication endpoints (login, OAuth start and callback, as in auth/router.py) are the deliberate exception: they run without a current account.

docs.title: API-4 · Hardcode instead of accept-then-reject
docs.text: If an enum field has a small, known value set and this endpoint will only ever accept one value, remove the field (or path segment) and hardcode the value. Keep the field and validate when the set is open-ended or expected to grow at this endpoint. Removing a field changes the API shape; grep callers and tests.

docs.title: API-5 · Don't expose internal integer ids for entities with a public_id
docs.text: Entities with a public_id are addressed by it outside the module, in paths, request bodies and responses. Response builders substitute the related row's public_id for its integer foreign key (MDL-5).

docs.title: API-6 · Request bodies reuse model schemas
docs.text: See MDL-3 and MDL-4. Router-only request classes are the exception and live in the entity's model file.

docs.title: ARC-1 · core never imports feature modules
docs.text: core/ is standalone. Feature modules under modules/ may depend on core; the reverse is never allowed. See also Dependency boundaries.

docs.title: ARC-2 · Hard dependencies on other modules are declared and few
docs.text:
Every module depends on msflib core, and on msflib-tenancy when it has tenant_id foreign keys (MDL-6). A module may also hard-depend on another module when it genuinely needs it to work, for example documents on ingestion or knowledge on documents. Such a dependency is declared in the module's pyproject.toml, and only declared dependencies are imported at module scope.

Before adding a new hard dependency, check whether the coupling can be optional instead. Integrate with modules a module can work without through:

  • structural Protocol contracts in contracts/,
  • injected callables (embedder, LLM and vector-store factories, as in ai_api's lazy callable factories),
  • eventbus hooks (ARC-4),
  • optional integrations/ packages guarded by is_importable (DEP-2).

docs.title: ARC-3 · Respect the layering
docs.text:
router.py  →  deps.py / services/access.py  →  services/  →  actions.py  →  database
Layer Owns Never router.py HTTP shape, status codes, wiring dependencies business rules, SQL, transaction composition deps.py request-scoped resolution: principal, path-param → row, access-checked context objects persistence services/ business rules, validation, orchestration, external calls building SQL actions.py queries and writes through ModelAction domain policy (SVC-2)

The router should look the same whether or not a service composes several actions internally.

docs.title: ARC-4 · Integrate across modules through lifecycle events
docs.text: Prefer listening to another module's ModelAction lifecycle events (for example documentrecord-update-post-commit) over importing its services.

docs.title: ARC-5 · Relationship() only to tables the module can always import
docs.text: Relationships are allowed between tables owned by the same module, and to tables of a declared hard dependency (ARC-2), for example workspace_notifications mapping notifications' Notification. Foreign keys to a module that is optional or undeclared stay plain columns with explicit fetches: a relationship would force that module to be importable whenever the model is. Reference: modules/conversation/msflib/conversation/models/.

docs.title: ARC-6 · Fix shared gaps at the root
docs.text:
When several modules need the same helper or workaround, put it in core and use it everywhere instead of adding a module-local copy. Examples: BaseEnum.__str__/__format__ (fixed in core rather than per-module .value guards), msflib.core.import_tools, msflib.actions.emit_after_commit.

Why: local workarounds multiply. Four modules had independently written the same enum-formatting guard before it was fixed once in core.

docs.title: ARC-7 · Avoid duplication; reuse shared stacks
docs.text: Reuse the shared AI core, retrieval adapters, vector-store factory and scope metadata helpers. Keep ai_api/ai_core integration composition-based so middleware, policy and adapters can change without rewrites.

docs.title: SCP-1 · Scope is a core concern
docs.text:
Scope lives in core/msflib/scope/. Use the canonical dimensions: tenant_id (organisation), account_id (user), and optional workspace_id. Use the existing scope compiler, policy and retrieval-filter adapters; don't build parallel scope implementations.

A scope is the server-decided place a request runs, identified by those dimensions: it bounds which data is visible and what the actor may do. It is not a client selector (SCP-3) and not a row fact such as who defined a role or where a grant applies; those keep their own types even when the fields match. ScopeEnvelope is the boundary and policy form. Code that filters or authorizes uses a typed scope (SCP-4).

docs.title: SCP-2 · None is a real scope bucket
docs.text: workspace_id=None means "workspace-agnostic", a valid hard boundary, not "unscoped". Preserve explicit-null semantics when compiling and filtering.

docs.title: SCP-3 · Identity is bound server-side; selectors are authorized
docs.text:
The isolation and identity dimensions (tenant_id, workspace_id, account_id) come from the server-side request context: the authenticated principal and the host app's resolvers. They are never taken from a client payload, a model or an agent tool argument.

Resource selectors that narrow the scope, such as conversation_id and sub_thread_id in ai_api's requests, may come from the validated request, but they must pass an access check for the current principal before they are used (as conversation's ai_bridge access dependency does). A model or tool output never supplies either kind.

Resolvers decide which tenant or workspace a request runs in; they do not check membership. A router or guard that needs it takes MembershipCheck callbacks (msflib.scope), one for the tenant and one for the workspace, supplied by the owning module and passed in by the host. It uses them for the caller (403) and for any account the request names (404). Don't fall back to a default tenant or to "any account" when a check is missing; a host that wants that passes allow_any_member.

docs.title: SCP-4 · Compile scope once, through the module's profile
docs.text: Register profiles in scope_profiles.py via ProfileRegistry with namespaced names ("<module>.<operation>"). Build the typed scope from the ScopeEnvelope with ScopeFactory.build(envelope, ScopeType, operation=...), once, at the request boundary, and pass it unchanged to every call below. TenantScope (tenant_id, workspace_id) is the shared shape: a module needing more dimensions subclasses it and does not redeclare the identity pair. Filter on the typed object, never on raw ScopeEnvelope.get_dim(...) calls, and don't parse dimension strings by hand. The type shares fields, not match semantics; an equality or hierarchical match belongs to the action method. Reference: knowledge/planner/scope_rewriter.py with contracts.KnowledgeScope, and ai_core/services/scope_metadata.py.

docs.title: Dependencies and packaging
docs.text: Installation, editable installs and release pinning are described in Development environment and Releases. The rules below cover how code takes on dependencies.

docs.title: DEP-1 · Optional third-party packages
docs.text:
1. Declare the package optional = true in the module's pyproject.toml and add it to [tool.poetry.extras].
  2. Load it through msflib.core.import_tools.import_optional(...), giving feature, pip_package, extra and distribution. Use is_importable(...) for availability probes.
  3. Document the extra in the module README's optional-extras table (see modules/ai_core/README.md).

docs.title: DEP-2 · Optional integrations with other modules
docs.text:
Code that uses another msflib module optionally lives in integrations/, checks availability with is_importable("msflib.<other>...") and imports inside the function. It is never exported from the package's lazy __getattr__.

Known gap

documents' optional Drivelink integration predates this rule: it lives in documents/drivelink/, imports msflib.drivelink at module scope, and register_event_hooks is exported through documents/__init__.py's lazy __getattr__. Moving it to integrations/ changes an import path, so it needs its own change (STY-4).

docs.title: DEP-3 · Reinstall touched packages when imports look stale
docs.text: Use scripts/install_modules.py --modules <names> for the packages you changed; don't modify the installer. See Stale installed copies.

docs.title: DEP-4 · Pin to release tags
docs.text: Dependencies on core and other modules are pinned to release tags, never rev = "dev". Declare release bumps as described in Releases.

docs.title: MDL-1 · Use the msflib base classes
docs.text:
Tables extend ModelBase (id, timestamps, lifecycle events). Every new schema extends SchemaBase, never pydantic's bare BaseModel, including request fragments and response contracts with no table behind them. Enums extend BaseEnum.

Known gap

Some existing schemas predate this rule and still extend BaseModel: documents/schema.py, ingestion/schema.py, ai_api/schema.py, ai_api/contracts.py, ai_core/policy.py and drivelink/models/validation.py. Don't migrate them as a side effect of other work (STY-6); new schemas in those modules still follow this rule.

docs.title: MDL-2 · Schemas live next to their table
docs.text:
models/<entity>.py holds the table and its Create/Update/Read schemas, which are the ModelAction generic parameters. A request class that doesn't match one table's CRUD shape (a composite request, or a narrow slice of a shared Update) still lives in the file of the entity it is about. Don't add a cross-entity schema.py; when reworking a module that has one, delete it once nothing in it lacks a model-file home. Existing schema.py files (see the MDL-1 note) are not moved as a side effect of other work.

Shared column groups go in SchemaBase mixins (AccountFieldsMixin, KnowledgeScopeMixin).

docs.title: MDL-3 · Create/Update hold only caller-supplied fields
docs.text:
Anything the server derives — principal, path-resolved ids, tenant/workspace scope, computed defaults, timestamps, counters — stays off the schema, even as an optional field. Pass it through action.create(..., update={...}) or action.update(..., update={...}) at the call site.

Why: a field that every caller overwrites still appears in the OpenAPI contract and invites clients to rely on it. Update schemas shared by several operations (rename, archive, change visibility) don't need narrowing to one caller's fields.

docs.title: MDL-4 · Don't add a DTO that restates Create/Update
docs.text: Use the model's Create/Update as the request body, or subclass it to add one or two genuinely request-only fields. Reference: conversation/models/resource_link.py::ResourceLinkCreate, used directly by the router.

docs.title: MDL-5 · One Read per entity, and only when something uses it
docs.text: A single XxxRead per entity serves both internal code and the HTTP response. Build responses with XxxRead.model_validate(row).model_copy(update={...}), overriding only derived fields such as a related row's public_id. Don't define Read classes speculatively; an unused Read is dead code.

docs.title: MDL-6 · Scope columns
docs.text:
• Always-scoped rows: tenant_id: int = Field(foreign_key="tenant.id", index=True), not null, no default. Add msflib-tenancy as a dependency.
  • Sometimes-scoped rows: tenant_id: int | None = Field(default=None, foreign_key="tenant.id", index=True); null means not tenant-scoped.
  • workspace_id: int | None, where None is a valid bucket (SCP-2).
  • Import the tenant model as msflib.tenancy.models.tenant.Tenant.

docs.title: MDL-7 · Don't denormalise scope columns without a query that needs them
docs.text: If a child table's queries really need scope columns, denormalise every dimension they filter on, never tenant alone. Otherwise the parent foreign key is the single source of truth, and the few queries that need scope join to the parent. Symmetric precedent: KnowledgeScopeMixin.

docs.title: MDL-8 · Use portable column types
docs.text: Use sqlalchemy.JSON, not JSONB, unless a Postgres-only feature is required; tests run on SQLite.

docs.title: MDL-9 · Relationship() fields
docs.text:
• Allowed within the module and to a declared hard dependency (ARC-5).
  • A file with a Relationship() must not use from __future__ import annotations. Use quoted forward references: thread: Optional["ConversationThread"] = Relationship(). Import the related class under TYPE_CHECKING if needed to break a cycle.
  • Add many-to-one sides only. Don't add collection sides on hot tables (Conversation.messages); paginate through the action instead.

Why: see Known pitfalls.

docs.title: MDL-10 · Format enums directly
docs.text: BaseEnum renders its plain value through str() and f-strings, whether the attribute holds a live enum member or a plain string after a flush. Write f"{row.kind}". Don't add .value or hasattr(x, "value") guards in new code. Compare a field against members of its own enum type, not another enum that happens to share values.

docs.title: Module authoring
docs.text: How to scaffold, install and register a module is in Adding a module. This page covers how the code inside msflib/<name>/ is organised.

docs.title: MOD-1 · Use the standard package layout
docs.text:
msflib/<name>/
  __init__.py         # empty, or lazy __getattr__ (MOD-2)
  config.py           # <Name>Settings(ModuleSettingsBase), ClassVar namespace
  models/             # one file per entity: table + its Create/Update/Read schemas
  actions.py          # all database access (SVC-1); a package if it grows
  services/           # business logic (SVC-*)
  eventbus/           # EventName enum + typed event contracts (MOD-5)
  contracts/          # Protocols and type aliases for cross-module structural typing
  deps.py             # request-scoped FastAPI dependencies (API-2), if needed
  router.py           # only if the module exposes HTTP endpoints
  scope_profiles.py   # if the module registers scope profiles (SCP-4)
  integrations/       # optional integrations with other modules (DEP-2)
  tests/
  <special>/          # registries, compilers, planners, parsers, adapters (MOD-4)

Reference: modules/conversation/msflib/conversation/, modules/documents/msflib/documents/.

docs.title: MOD-2 · __init__.py never imports eagerly
docs.text:
Keep it empty, or use a lazy __getattr__ map with absolute msflib.<name>.… paths:

def __getattr__(name: str) -> Any:
    mapping = {"FooAction": ("msflib.foo.actions", "FooAction")}
    if name not in mapping:
        raise AttributeError(f"module {__name__!r} has no attribute {name!r}")
    module_name, attr_name = mapping[name]
    return getattr(import_module(module_name), attr_name)

An unknown name must raise AttributeError, not KeyError, so hasattr() and failing from msflib.foo import x imports behave normally. Reference: documents/__init__.py.

Why: the namespace package is importable under several sys.path entries. Eager model imports register SQLModel tables twice ("Table already defined") and pull optional dependencies in at import time.

docs.title: MOD-3 · Business logic lives in services/ (plural)
docs.text: Every module, and the module template, uses services/. Modules that used to have service/ keep it as a deprecated alias package that re-exports services/ and warns on import. Don't add code to a service/ alias or import from it; the aliases will be removed in a future minor release.

docs.title: MOD-4 · Special logic gets its own package
docs.text:
Registries, compilers, planners, parsers and adapters, meaning logic that is neither CRUD nor orchestration, go in dedicated packages (documents/adapters/, ai_core/services/chunking/, knowledge/planner/). New registries follow the ChunkingRegistry shape: register, resolve, list, with capability records.

Don't create a package or module for a one-line helper. A helper reused at least three times within one file may become a private function in that file.

docs.title: MOD-5 · Eventbus layout
docs.text:
• eventbus/events.py holds EventName(BaseEnum), typed EventOptions contracts and an EVENT_CONTRACTS map.
  • Emit with msflib.eventbus.emitter.emit_optional(EventName.X, subject, options).
  • Don't re-emit what ModelAction lifecycle events already cover. Module events are for domain moments (knowledge-fragment-ingested, account-created-pre-email).
  • Events tied to an uncommitted write use emit_after_commit (SVC-10).

docs.title: MOD-6 · Settings are scoped
docs.text: config.py defines <Name>Settings(ModuleSettingsBase) with a ClassVar namespace. Classes that need settings receive them in __init__ and call settings.scope("<NAMESPACE>").

docs.title: MOD-7 · Background pipelines register with msflib.ingestion
docs.text: Any fetch → transform → persist background flow registers a pipeline_kind with msflib.ingestion instead of building its own queue. Follow modules/ingestion/README.md ("Adding a new pipeline kind" and "Wiring into a host app"). Examples: msflib.documents.services.pipeline (simple stage singleton) and msflib.knowledge.integrations.pipeline (stage built by a factory because it needs a constructed KnowledgeEngine).

docs.title: MOD-8 · Keep the module's docs current
docs.text: When capabilities change, update the module README.md (what it owns, layout, usage snippets, boundaries, status) and its page under docs/modules/. See Writing docs.

docs.title: Known pitfalls
docs.text: Problems that have already cost debugging time. Each entry gives the symptom, the cause and the fix.

docs.title: Relationship and PEP 563
docs.text:
Symptom: InvalidRequestError: ... failed to locate a name ('X | None') on the first instantiation of a model, not at import or create_all().

Cause: from __future__ import annotations turns the annotation into a string that SQLAlchemy's class registry can't resolve.

Fix: follow MDL-9: no future import in that file, quoted forward references. create_all() passing does not prove the mapping works.

docs.title: SQLite savepoints do not roll back
docs.text:
Symptom: after session.begin_nested() and a later session.rollback(), the row is still there.

Cause: pysqlite's own transaction handling commits the savepoint.

Fix: wrap the engine with core's helper, which installs the workaround once (TST-2):

from msflib.db.sqlite import enable_savepoints

engine = enable_savepoints(
    create_engine("sqlite://", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False}, poolclass=StaticPool)
)

Don't hand-write the pysqlite event listeners in a fixture.

docs.title: Tables defined twice
docs.text:
Symptom: Table '...' is already defined for this MetaData instance.

Cause: a module __init__.py imports models eagerly, and the namespace package is loaded through two sys.path entries.

Fix: MOD-2.

docs.title: Tests run old code
docs.text:
Symptom: a change has no effect in tests, or an import that exists in the source is missing.

Cause: a non-editable copy in site-packages shadows the workspace.

Fix: see Stale installed copies.

docs.title: Relationship access after commit
docs.text:
Symptom: DetachedInstanceError when reading a relationship on a row that a committing action (for example delete_by_all) already returned.

Fix: use a row you already hold in the request context instead of the detached row's relationship.

docs.title: Recursive default construction
docs.text:
Symptom: RecursionError when constructing an action or service.

Cause: x or XAction() defaults in __init__ that construct back to the original class.

Fix: SVC-7.

docs.title: HookRegistry.bind() does not register listeners
docs.text:
Symptom: a listener registered in __init__ never fires.

Cause: bind() only records the binding so it can be replaced later.

Fix: call emitter.on(...) (or use @emitter.listen) and then bind(). See workspaces/eventbus/__init__.py.

docs.title: Missing-package tests stop covering the probe
docs.text:
Symptom: after moving to is_importable, a "package missing" test crashes during loading instead of skipping.

Fix: TST-7: patch is_importable consistently with the faked import.

docs.title: Readiness checks
docs.text: Rules for the readiness engine (msflib.core.readiness) and for the checks and remedies that modules ship in <module>.readiness. They come from the review of the engine's first pull request, where each rule was a finding that cost a review round. Integration documentation is in Readiness.

docs.title: RDY-1 · A check observes; a remedy fixes, safely
docs.text: A check never changes anything. A remedy is idempotent and declares its safety. A remedy that can lose data is guidance only and is never applied by --fix. safety has no default, so a remedy cannot be registered without classifying it. Anything the code cannot prove safe is manual: decide by an allowlist of what is understood, not by a list of what is known to be dangerous.

docs.title: RDY-2 · Never report green for something that was not verified
docs.text: A skipped, unconfigured or uninspectable requirement is a WARN or FAIL, never a quiet SKIP or PASS. Examples: an engine without a MigrationConfig, an ImportError while inspecting the schema, a requirement that is configured but incomplete (file storage with no path), an optional check that cannot read its table, a --settings run with no engine, a suite without an engine, --offline skipping a paid check, a check that does not compare columns. If the check cannot say, its detail says what it did not look at.

docs.title: RDY-3 · Offer only a remedy that can fix the finding
docs.text: Pass remedies=() when no remedy helps (the inspection itself failed or crashed, drift remains after a baseline would be stamped, a baseline is not configured). A remedy's ready() returns the reason it cannot run; the plan reports it. A check can only link a remedy that lists that check in its fixes.

docs.title: RDY-4 · Applicability has a fixed order
docs.text: Profile and --offline exclusion, then prerequisites (a failed prerequisite is BLOCKED, a skipped one is SKIP), then the when predicate. A predicate is cheap, runs under the check's timeout, and a predicate that raises is a failure. A False predicate settles the finding as SKIP, without running the check.

docs.title: RDY-5 · Assume a timed-out check keeps running
docs.text: Every check has a timeout, and a thread cannot be stopped. After a timeout the context is forked, plain data is copied and handles are shared, and the late output of the abandoned thread must not reach another check, a restored log handler or the JSON document. Do not add more global hooks to contain it; the planned replacement is a killable worker process (msflib/fastapi#331).

docs.title: RDY-6 · All output goes through masking
docs.text: Fetch secrets with ctx.get_secret, and mask text and structured data with msflib.core.pii (mask_text, mask_url, mask_value, SecretSet, mask_sensitive), never with a copy of that logic. Mask detail, steps, evidence, the log and the unattributed log. Nothing is printed to stdout in --json mode, which carries exactly one document: print and stderr output during a check or remedy is captured like logging (kept for --verbose, never a warning). A URL's password and its sensitively named query parameters are hidden; other credentials are registered as secrets. Longer secrets are replaced before shorter ones. ctx.get_secret(name, namespace=...) reads that module's scope only; a deployment variable that is not a module setting is read without a namespace.

docs.title: RDY-7 · The text, the JSON and the exit code say the same thing
docs.text: Everything that affects the verdict is a finding in the report, added before rendering (ids starting run. are reserved for these and a check cannot take one), not patched into the exit code afterwards. JSON fields are additive, documented, and always present ([] rather than omitted, also without --fix). fixes_applied lists only what ran; skipped and dry-run remedies are in fixes_not_applied with their state.

docs.title: RDY-8 · The migration gate is conservative and tracked
docs.text: core.migrate is applied automatically only when the pending revisions are shown not to lose data. The current scan reads the revision's Python and cannot be a proof; every bypass found in review (aliases, dynamic built-ins, helpers imported from other modules, literal SQL that is not DROP/DELETE) belongs in msflib/fastapi#330, which replaces it with a scan of the SQL Alembic renders offline. Do not patch the AST scan one bypass at a time.

docs.title: RDY-9 · Typed objects, lazy exports
docs.text: Outcomes use the Outcome verbs, step kinds and run states are enums, and reports are dataclasses, not strings and dicts (TYP-2). The package __init__.py is lazy (MOD-2) and imports nothing at runtime that is not a declared dependency (DEP-1). Names follow SDC-1–4.

docs.title: RDY-10 · Discovery never hides a module
docs.text: A module's registry is found from the composed settings, through Optional, X | None and Annotated at any depth. A module whose readiness fails to import, or has no registry, becomes a failing <module>.readiness.load check, never a missing one.

docs.title: RDY-11 · Tests prove the finding
docs.text: Each check has a pass, a fail and a skip test. Timing tests wait on events, not sleeps. Run the suite in an environment that has the optional dependencies (Alembic), because tests that import them skip without it and hide failures. Every review finding gets a regression test that fails first (TST-6).

docs.title: Vetting a readiness pull request
docs.text:
Before requesting review, walk the diff against this list. It is the set of questions the first pull request was asked, one by one.

  • [ ] Does any check change something, or any destructive remedy run in --fix? (RDY-1)
  • [ ] Can any path end READY without the requirement being checked? (RDY-2)
  • [ ] Does every failing check link only remedies that can fix it? (RDY-3)
  • [ ] Is each predicate cheap, and what happens when it raises or is false? (RDY-4)
  • [ ] What does the check write after its timeout? (RDY-5)
  • [ ] Does every check that cannot run without an engine or migration config declare needs=? (RDY-2)
  • [ ] Is every string that reaches the report masked, and does it use msflib.core.pii? (RDY-6)
  • [ ] Do the text, the JSON and the exit code agree for this change? (RDY-7)
  • [ ] Does it add a new way to approve a migration? Then it belongs in #330. (RDY-8)
  • [ ] Are outcomes, states and exports typed and lazy? (RDY-9)
  • [ ] Is the module's registry discovered, and what happens if it fails to load? (RDY-10)
  • [ ] Is there a test for each finding, run with Alembic installed? (RDY-11)

docs.title: Reviewing pull requests
docs.text: Branch, commit and CI conventions are in Commit and pull request conventions. PR descriptions follow the org template (REV-7).

docs.title: REV-1 · Review checklist
docs.text:
Cite rule IDs in review comments.

  • Boundaries: no core → module imports; module-scope imports only of declared dependencies; a new hard dependency is justified; no Relationship() to an optional module (ARC-1, ARC-2, ARC-5).
  • Layering: database access only in actions; actions free of domain policy; no transaction composition in routers (ARC-3, SVC-1, SVC-2, SVC-5).
  • Transactions: no undocumented commit passthrough on services; events tied to uncommitted writes are deferred (SVC-4, SVC-10).
  • Schemas: no server-derived fields on Create/Update; no duplicate DTOs or unused Reads (MDL-3, MDL-4, MDL-5).
  • Scope: identity dimensions server-bound, request selectors authorized; typed scope objects; null workspace preserved (SCP-2, SCP-3, SVC-3).
  • Typing: no new Any, getattr, or re-validation mid-path (TYP-2, TYP-3).
  • Readiness: checks and remedies in msflib.core.readiness follow the vetting list in Readiness checks (RDY-1–11).
  • Tests: behaviour change has tests; no live calls; regression test fails first (TST-4, TST-6).
  • Readability: names follow SDC-1–6; flags keyword-only (SDC-8).
  • Docs: module README and docs page updated (MOD-8).
  • Change policy: compatibility choice was confirmed; no speculative options; no unrelated changes (STY-4, STY-5, STY-6).

docs.title: REV-2 · Verify every automated finding against the code
docs.text:
Automated reviewers (Copilot, Gemini, Qodo, the repository's AI review action) misattribute files and lines, and sometimes describe code that doesn't exist. Before accepting or rejecting a finding:

  1. Read the code at the cited location.
  2. Check whether the finding contradicts a documented design decision (a docstring, a rule here, the module's architecture notes).
  3. Check the claim, and also whether the code it points at should exist at all. A finding can be wrong in its stated claim but still point at a real problem.

docs.title: REV-3 · Close every thread
docs.text: For each finding, either fix it, or reply explaining why it is not being changed, or defer it to a linked issue. Resolve the thread once done. Rejecting a finding needs the evidence (code or design reference), not just "not an issue".

docs.title: REV-4 · Fix the pattern, not just the instance
docs.text: When the same finding recurs across files, look for a shared primitive in core instead of patching each place (ARC-6). Example: repeated commit/event race findings led to emit_after_commit.

docs.title: REV-5 · Fix commits
docs.text: Address review feedback in focused commits whose message names what was fixed and, where useful, the rule ID. The code itself carries no review narration (STY-3).

docs.title: REV-6 · New conventions update these pages in the same PR
docs.text: When a review settles a new convention, add or amend the rule here in the same pull request.

docs.title: REV-7 · Pull request descriptions follow the org template
docs.text:
Every pull request, whether opened by a person or an agent, uses the organisation template from the msflib/.github repository (.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md). GitHub pre-fills it in the browser; when opening a PR from the command line, fetch it first:

gh api repos/msflib/.github/contents/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md --jq .content | base64 -d
  • Keep every section and every checklist item, in order. Summary leads with one or two sentences; supporting detail can follow as a short list.
  • Tick only the type-of-change and checklist items that are true. Leave the others unchecked; don't delete or annotate them.
  • A section that doesn't apply (Screenshots with no UI, Documentation when no docs changed) stays, with n/a under its heading.
  • The only section to remove is Release Notes, when the PR has no release:* label and won't trigger a release (see Releases).
  • How to test is written for a software tester: numbered steps they can follow on a fresh checkout (branch, setup, commands, what to open or click) and the expected result of each. Write n/a only when there is genuinely nothing to test.
  • Use Closes #N only when the PR completes the issue; otherwise Refs #N.
  • Report test results as they are, including unrelated failures and why they are unrelated (AGT-5).

docs.title: Self-documenting code
docs.text: Names and structure should explain the code so comments rarely have to (STY-2). A name is read in context: its package, module and class are part of it, so don't repeat them.

docs.title: SDC-1 · Module names: one word if possible, two at most
docs.text:
Name a module with a single word. Use two words joined by an underscore only when no single word conveys its purpose. Never use three or more.

conversation/services/access.py        # not conversation_access_service.py
documents/services/uploads.py          # not document_upload_handler.py
ai_core/services/scope_metadata.py     # two words: no single word fits

Packages that hold several things of one kind are plural (services/, models/, contracts/). Test modules are exempt: test_<subject>.py may be as long as the subject needs (see TST-8).

docs.title: SDC-2 · Functions and methods: active verbs, as few words as stay clear
docs.text:
Start with a verb in the active form (resolve_conversation, post, archive). One word is best when it is clear from the name and its context; two to four words are acceptable, but each extra word needs more justification. Don't repeat the class or module name: MessageAction.post, not MessageAction.post_message.

Use verbs consistently:

Verb Meaning get one item by id or key; returns None if missing list many items, possibly paginated find search by criteria; empty result is normal require like get, but raises if missing or not allowed resolve derive a value from context, defaults or fallbacks build construct an object without persisting it create persist a new row ensure create if missing, idempotent validate raise if invalid; returns nothing or the validated value register, emit registry and eventbus operations on_<event> event listener

Predicates return bool and read as questions: is_active_member, has_owner, can_post.

Exceptions: test functions are exempt from the length limit; they follow TST-8. Router and dependency factories follow the existing FastAPI style (router(), get_<module>_dependencies()). Methods implementing a third-party protocol keep that protocol's names (similarity_search).

docs.title: SDC-3 · Variables: nouns, two words at most
docs.text:
Name the thing the variable holds, in at most two words (membership, root_message). Booleans read as predicates (is_archived). Collections are plural (messages); mappings are named for their values, with the key when it matters (members_by_id).

  • Don't encode the type in the name (message_list, data_dict).
  • Single letters only for short loop indices, comprehensions and maths.
  • No abbreviations beyond the well-known (id, db, url, llm).
  • Put the unit in the name when the type doesn't carry it (timeout_seconds).

docs.title: SDC-4 · Classes: UpperCamelCase nouns that say what the class is
docs.text:
ConversationThread, ChunkingRegistry, MemberEligibility. Avoid vague suffixes such as Manager, Helper, Utils, Handler and Impl. Use the established role suffixes:

Role Pattern Action class <Entity>Action Service class <Domain>Service Module settings <Module>Settings Schemas <Entity>Create, <Entity>Update, <Entity>Read Abstract base <Thing>Base Exception <Problem>Error

Enums are singular nouns (MemberKind, SenderKind).

docs.title: SDC-5 · One name per concept
docs.text: Use the same term for the same thing across modules and layers: don't call it account in one layer and user in another, or rename data to payload halfway down a call chain. Name constructor arguments for what they actually hold (SVC-6).

docs.title: SDC-6 · Constants and private names
docs.text: Constants are UPPER_SNAKE_CASE. Module-internal helpers and attributes start with an underscore and are not exported.

docs.title: SDC-7 · No magic values
docs.text: Give meaningful literals a name: a module constant, a setting, or a BaseEnum member instead of a bare string compared in several places.

docs.title: SDC-8 · Flags are keyword-only
docs.text: Boolean and option parameters go after * so calls read as create(session, data=..., commit=False), never create(session, data, False).

docs.title: SDC-9 · Extract instead of explaining
docs.text: If a block needs a comment to say what it does, move it into a function whose name says it. Keep a function at one level of abstraction, and prefer early returns to deep nesting.

docs.title: SDC-10 · Type hints are part of the documentation
docs.text: Annotate every public signature, including return types. A precise type (ConversationScope, MessageCreate) documents the contract better than a docstring describing a dict.

docs.title: SDC-11 · Docstrings state what the name can't
docs.text: Add a short docstring to a public function or class when its contract isn't obvious from the name and types: what it raises, whether it commits, which events it emits, what it returns on a miss. Don't restate the signature.

docs.title: STY-1 · Lint and format with the repository config
docs.text: Ruff (check and format) and flake8 run through pre-commit and CI. See Linting and typing.

docs.title: STY-2 · Self-documenting code first; short comments
docs.text: Prefer names and structure that explain the code (see Self-documenting code). Don't add comments that restate the code. A comment on a single field or statement is one short line. Module and class docstrings may carry longer rationale: invariants, concurrency notes, why the code lives where it does.

docs.title: STY-3 · Comments describe the code, not its history
docs.text: When fixing review feedback, don't narrate the review thread or the replaced approach in a comment. Write any comment as if explaining the code to a new reader; the commit message carries the "addresses review" context.

docs.title: STY-4 · Ask before choosing compatibility shim or clean break
docs.text:
When changing a public API, setting or schema, ask the maintainer whether to add a compatibility layer (alias, deprecated fallback, transitional parameter) or make a clean break that updates all callers. Don't decide silently either way.

Most modules are pre-production, so the usual answer is a clean break: no aliases, no deprecated fallbacks, callers and tests updated in the same change. Revisit this rule at 1.0.

docs.title: STY-5 · No speculative flexibility
docs.text: Don't add parameters, flags or extension points for hypothetical callers (commit: bool "just in case", unused options). Add them when a real caller needs them.

docs.title: STY-6 · Stay in scope
docs.text: Don't fix unrelated problems in modules you happen to touch. Note them and propose a separate change (issue or PR). Exception: simplifying an outdated pattern in code you are already editing for the task.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Commands and suite layout are in Running tests.

docs.title: TST-1 · Run the narrowest suite that proves the change
docs.text: Use the repository virtual environment (.venv/bin/pytest). Run the touched module first, then widen. Run each module suite and testsite in separate pytest processes. Keep the complete failure output when reporting.

docs.title: TST-2 · Module conftest.py shape
docs.text:
• In-memory SQLite: create_engine("sqlite://", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False}, poolclass=StaticPool), wrapped with msflib.db.sqlite.enable_savepoints(engine) so savepoints roll back correctly (see Known pitfalls), plus SQLModel.metadata.create_all.
  • Import the module's models for table registration (import msflib.<name>.models # noqa: F401).
  • A module with tenant_id foreign keys (MDL-6) also imports the tenant table explicitly, because msflib.tenancy.models deliberately doesn't re-export it: from msflib.tenancy.models.tenant import Tenant # noqa: F401.

docs.title: TST-3 · Exercise actions and services with realistic data
docs.text: Fixtures provide action instances, service instances and ScopeEnvelopes, and persist real rows through actions. Avoid hardcoded ids and mock-style setup. For tables with server-derived fields, prefer action.create(session, data=action.random(), update={...}) over create_random(**overrides), which can't set fields outside the schema.

docs.title: TST-4 · Unit tests never call live services
docs.text: Stub LLM resolution, external APIs and brokers. A test that passes only when a live provider is reachable is a bug in the test. Tests that need live backends use the integration marker or a RUN_LIVE_* environment gate.

docs.title: TST-5 · A pre-existing failure is still a failure
docs.text: Showing that a test also fails without your change (for example with git stash) proves you didn't cause it, not that it's fine. Find the cause, then fix it or report it.

docs.title: TST-6 · Regression tests must fail first
docs.text: For a bug fix, confirm the new test fails on the old code and passes on the fix.

docs.title: TST-7 · Keep test doubles aligned with the code path
docs.text: When patching a module's import to simulate a missing package, also patch the is_importable/import_optional call it now goes through. When production code replaces a helper, update the nearby tests and mock assertions in the same change.

docs.title: TST-8 · Test names describe the behaviour
docs.text: Test functions and test modules are exempt from the naming length limits in SDC-1 and SDC-2. Name a test for the behaviour it checks, as test_<subject>_<behaviour>[_<condition>], so a failure reads as a sentence: test_agent_stream_writes_partial_transcript_on_stream_failure.

docs.title: TYP-1 · Use the core typing helpers
docs.text: Use msflib.core.typing for coercion, validation and nullability handling. If a capability is missing, add it there rather than writing a one-off helper in a module (ARC-6).

docs.title: TYP-2 · Typed objects over loose data
docs.text: Use frozen dataclasses, SchemaBase schemas and Protocols in signatures. Avoid Any, Mapping[str, Any] parameters on internal paths, and getattr()/hasattr() where a type or protocol can state the dependency.

docs.title: TYP-3 · Validate once at the boundary, then trust the type
docs.text: After an object is validated (pydantic model, profile validation, IR validation pass), don't re-check it mid-path, especially on hot paths. Don't guard against states the types make impossible, such as or [] on a field that is always a list.

docs.title: TYP-4 · Project untyped sources into a contract at the boundary
docs.text: When a source produces loosely typed data, convert it once into a typed contract that downstream code uses directly. Reference: ScopeCompiler output projected into knowledge.contracts.KnowledgeScope.

docs.title: TYP-5 · Legitimate exceptions
docs.text:
• validating untrusted input (LLM output, external payloads),
  • reflection for schema or tool generation (dataclasses.fields),
  • the lazy __getattr__ module pattern (MOD-2),
  • duck-typed third-party objects with no contract yet; add a Protocol in contracts/ as soon as a second call site needs it.

docs.title: TYP-6 · Annotation style
docs.text: Use PEP 604 unions and builtin generics (X | None, list[X]). Model files with Relationship() fields are the exception (MDL-9).

docs.title: Diving deeper
docs.text:
These guides are for developers who already have a FastAPI host app, or are building one, and want to use the MSFLib packages in it. They are task-oriented. Each one shows a small example that was run against the current source, and says so when a technique is not supported.

If you have not yet read Basics and the other quick-start pages, start there. The guides assume you know what a module, an action and a router factory are.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text: How to extend MSFLib explains the extension model: what the packages provide, what your app owns, and which guide to read for each kind of change. It also lists the techniques that do not work.

docs.title: Guides by task
docs.text: I want to Read Add my own tables, actions, endpoints and settings next to MSFLib modules Writing custom code Mount a module's endpoints at my own prefix, with my own dependencies, or hide or replace some of them Mounting routes Add columns to a module's account, profile or workspace table, or change its request and response schemas Overriding models Add business rules, queries or hooks around create, update and delete Subclassing actions Sign users in, protect routes, and resolve the active workspace Authentication Run ingestion and other background work outside the request Long-running jobs and ingestion Use chat models, embeddings, chunking and vector search AI capabilities Know before traffic arrives which requirements are met (database, broker, worker, providers) and fix what is not Readiness checks

docs.title: Suggested order for a new host app
docs.text:
1. Writing custom code builds a complete small host app (settings, models, an action, an authenticated router, a test). Every later guide reuses its pieces.
  2. Authentication covers the login flow that the example relies on, plus workspaces.
  3. Overriding models, Subclassing actions and Mounting routes as you need to bend a module to your product.

docs.title: Related material
docs.text:
• Concepts describes the ideas behind the packages: tiered configuration, policy, scopes, the event bus and dependency injection.
  • Modules has one page per package with its settings, models, actions and routers.
  • Contributors working inside this repository should also read Contributing.

docs.title: AI capabilities
docs.text:
This guide walks through the AI building blocks in msflib-ai-core: getting a chat model and embeddings, chunking documents, storing and searching them with tenant isolation, versioning prompts, and tracking usage. Each section is short and builds on the previous one.

All imports come from subpackages. msflib.ai_core itself exports nothing.

docs.title: 1. Settings
docs.text:
AICoreSettings holds the provider, model and key fields. In a host app it is read from the AI_CORE namespace of your settings (see the environment variable rules on the module page). For scripts and tests you can construct it directly:

from msflib.ai_core.config import AICoreSettings

ai_settings = AICoreSettings(
    LLM_PROVIDER="openai",
    LLM_MODEL="gpt-4o",
    LLM_API_KEY="sk-...",
    EMBEDDING_API_KEY="sk-...",
    VECTOR_STORE_URL="postgresql+psycopg://user:password@localhost:5432/app",
)

In a host app, pass settings.scope("AI_CORE") (it works for composed and subclassed settings) or use get_ai_dependencies(settings).get_llm(); do not pass the host settings object itself, which raises AttributeError when the settings are composed. The snippets below use the standalone ai_settings.

VECTOR_STORE_URL is only needed for section 4. The default pgvector backend raises ValueError: VECTOR_STORE_URL is required for pgvector backend without it, and so do qdrant, weaviate and milvus. Pinecone needs VECTOR_STORE_API_KEY instead, and chroma and faiss need neither.

Provider names are plain strings, validated against the provider type registry. The registry mirrors the providers your installed langchain supports (for example openai, azure_openai, anthropic, groq, ollama), and each needs its package installed (see the extras table on the module page). List them with get_provider_type_registry().names() from msflib.ai_core.providers.

docs.title: 2. A chat model and embeddings
docs.text:
The next snippet needs the openai extra.

from msflib.ai_core.providers import get_embeddings, get_llm

llm = get_llm(ai_settings)
reply = llm.invoke("Summarise MSFLib in one sentence.")
print(reply.content)

embeddings = get_embeddings(ai_settings)
vector = embeddings.embed_query("hello")

get_llm and get_embeddings return the underlying langchain objects, so streaming (llm.stream(...)), batching and the rest of the langchain API work unchanged. To use another provider, change LLM_PROVIDER and LLM_MODEL, for example "anthropic" with an Anthropic model id (install the anthropic extra). Embeddings are configured separately with EMBEDDING_PROVIDER and EMBEDDING_MODEL, and Anthropic offers no embeddings.

In a host app, prefer the registry-aware variants on the dependency namespace (get_llm_from_registry(session, scope=scope)), which pick a database-backed provider profile for the caller's tenant, workspace or user before falling back to settings. See get_ai_dependencies on the module page.

docs.title: 3. Chunking documents
docs.text:
IngestionPipeline loads, cleans and chunks a document and returns the chunks with metadata.

from msflib.ai_core.services.ingestion_pipeline import IngestionPipeline

pipeline = IngestionPipeline()

result = pipeline.ingest(
    {
        "format": "markdown",
        "content": "# Refunds\n\nRefunds take 5 days.\n\n## Exceptions\n\nGift cards are final sale.",
        "source_id": "faq-1",
    }
)

for chunk in result.chunks:
    print(chunk.metadata["chunk_index"], chunk.text)

result also reports which chunking strategy ran (result.chunk_strategy) and whether it came from the built-in fallback provider (result.fallback_used; the default markdown strategy is a fallback-provider strategy, so this is True in the example above and does not signal an error).

You can pick the strategy and size per call:

long_text = "refund policy " * 400

result = pipeline.ingest(
    long_text,
    source_type="text",
    strategy_name="token_window",
    chunk_options={"chunk_size": 200, "chunk_overlap": 30},
)

Default embedder and indexer are placeholders

Without arguments, IngestionPipeline uses a deterministic stand-in embedder and an indexer that only returns ids like chunk-0. They exist for wiring and tests. For real retrieval, either pass your own embedder= and indexer= callables, or take result.chunks[i].text and store them yourself as shown in the next section. An embedder is embedder(texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]; an indexer is indexer(records: list[dict]) -> list[str], where each record has text, embedding and metadata.

Other constructor arguments (loaders=, cleaner=, chunking_registry=) and per-call workspace_settings= / chunking_policy= let you add loaders and tune strategy selection. Custom chunking strategies and document loaders are covered in the chunking and extraction READMEs under modules/ai_core/msflib/ai_core/services/.

docs.title: 4. Storing and searching with tenant isolation
docs.text:
This section continues from sections 1 to 3 (ai_settings, embeddings and result). It needs the pgvector extra and a Postgres database with the vector extension.

from msflib.ai_core.vector_store import get_vector_store, similarity_search_scoped
from msflib.scope import build_context_scope

store = get_vector_store(ai_settings, "faq", embeddings)

store.add_texts(
    [chunk.text for chunk in result.chunks],
    metadatas=[
        {"tenant_id": "1", "workspace_id": "7", "source_id": "faq-1"}
        for _ in result.chunks
    ],
)

scope = build_context_scope(tenant_id=1, workspace_id=7)
hits = similarity_search_scoped(store, query="How long do refunds take?", scope=scope, k=4)

Points to know:

  • get_vector_store returns a ScopedVectorStore. It supports similarity_search, add_texts, add_documents, delete and close. The native langchain store is available as store.raw.
  • Always search with similarity_search_scoped in multi-tenant code. It builds mandatory tenant and workspace metadata filters from the ScopeEnvelope. Calling store.similarity_search(...) directly applies no filter.
  • Write dimension values as strings ("1", not 1), because build_context_scope stringifies them.
  • The metadata you write must carry the dimensions the filter reads. tenant_id and workspace_id are required, exact-match string values; a scope with no workspace matches only content written with no workspace. Conversation, sub-thread and private-account dimensions are optional: content written without conversation_id, sub_thread_id or private_to_account_id is treated as shared across the workspace, so tag anything that belongs to a single conversation, sub-thread or account. Write through the ScopedVectorStore, not store.raw: on backends without native missing-key filters (Pinecone, Chroma, Milvus) it adds the __null__ markers that make untagged content visible as shared. build_retrieval_filters(scope=scope) shows exactly what a search requires.
  • Collection names are "<VECTOR_STORE_COLLECTION_PREFIX>_<name>", sanitised for the backend. The prefix organises collections; it does not isolate tenants. Isolation comes from the metadata filters.
  • The default backend is pgvector (extras = ["pgvector"], and CREATE EXTENSION vector; once on the database). Qdrant, Pinecone, Chroma, Weaviate, Milvus and FAISS are also supported (each has an extra of the same name); set VECTOR_STORE_BACKEND.

docs.title: 5. Versioned prompts
docs.text:
PromptRegistryService stores prompt versions in the database and resolves the active one by scope, in the order user, then workspace, then global.

The examples below assume session is an open SQLModel Session from your host app (for instance the one injected by your get_session dependency), and that the ai_prompt_version table exists. Import msflib.tenancy.models.tenant before SQLModel.metadata.create_all (or your migrations), because ai-core's provider and vector-store profile tables reference tenant; see the known issue on the module page.

from msflib.ai_core.services.prompt_registry import PromptRegistryService

prompts = PromptRegistryService()

prompts.register(session, "support.system", "v1", "You are a helpful assistant.", set_active=True)
prompts.register(
    session, "support.system", "v2", "You are concise.", workspace_id=5, set_active=True
)

prompts.get_active_version(session, "support.system").content
# 'You are a helpful assistant.'
prompts.get_active_version(session, "support.system", workspace_id=5).content
# 'You are concise.'

Registering the same key, version and scope twice raises PromptVersionConflictError. To roll a prompt out without a deploy, register a new version and activate it with set_active. A user-level override uses both workspace_id and account_id.

docs.title: 6. Usage tracking and rate limiting
docs.text:
from msflib.ai_core.providers import get_llm
from msflib.ai_core.tracking.usage import TokenUsageCallback

llm = get_llm(ai_settings)
usage = TokenUsageCallback(workspace_id="7")
llm.invoke("Hello", config={"callbacks": [usage]})
print(usage.prompt_tokens, usage.completion_tokens, usage.total_tokens)

The callback accumulates token counts across every call it is attached to, so create one per request. Streaming responses only report usage if the provider includes it. On every model call it also emits ai_core.token_usage on the event bus, but only if a listener is registered. Register it on the app emitter with @app_emitter.on("ai_core.token_usage") (app_emitter = bind_app_emitter(app)). It fires for model calls made inside a request (including BackgroundTasks); in threads or scripts in the web process, wrap the call in with use_app_emitter(app):, otherwise the event goes to the default emitter and the listener never runs. A Celery task has no FastAPI app: register its listener on the worker's emitter, AppEmitter(get_emitter()) (both from msflib.eventbus). The payload (workspace_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, total_cost) carries the callback's running totals rather than per-call amounts. Use a fresh callback per request, or subtract the previous totals, before billing from it.

from msflib.ai_core.tracking.limiter import RateLimiter, RateLimitExceeded

limiter = RateLimiter(rpm=60, redis_url="redis://localhost:6379/0")

try:
    limiter.check("workspace:7")
except RateLimitExceeded:
    ...  # return HTTP 429

check raises RateLimitExceeded once a namespace makes more than rpm calls within the same clock minute (a fixed window, not a sliding one).
